Package backend

Class Sprite

java.lang.Object
backend.Sprite
public class Sprite extends Object
Represents a single sprite in the Scratch-like environment. A sprite has a position, direction, size, a set of costumes, and text state (say/think). Sprites can be cloned — each clone gets a unique instance ID but shares the same name. All coordinates use Scratch convention: origin at center, positive Y upward, with bounds roughly -240 to 240 on X and -180 to 180 on Y.

  • Constructor Details

    • Sprite

      public Sprite(String name, int x, int y, int size, ArrayList<File> costumes)
      Constructs a fully specified Sprite with a name, position, size, and costumes. The first costume in the list becomes the active costume. Direction defaults to 0 (facing right).
      Parameters:
      name - the display name of this sprite
      x - initial X position in Scratch coordinates
      y - initial Y position in Scratch coordinates
      size - initial size as a percentage (100 = normal size)
      costumes - list of costume image files; must not be null or empty

    • Sprite

      public Sprite(String name, ArrayList<File> costumes)
      Constructs a Sprite at the origin (0, 0) with default size 100.
      Parameters:
      name - the display name of this sprite
      costumes - list of costume image files

    • Sprite

      public Sprite(Sprite other)
      Copy constructor. Creates a deep copy of another sprite with a new unique instance ID. Used when creating clones — the clone shares the same name but is otherwise independent.
      Parameters:
      other - the Sprite to copy

    • move

      public void move(int steps)
      Moves the sprite forward by the given number of steps in the direction it is currently facing. Uses trigonometry to decompose the movement into X and Y components. Scratch's direction 0 = right (east), so the angle is rotated 90 degrees from standard math.
      Parameters:
      steps - number of steps to move

    • goTo

      Parameters:

      myY - target Y position in Scratch coordinates

    • isTouchingMouse

      public boolean isTouchingMouse(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Returns whether the mouse cursor is currently over this sprite. Uses the sprite's scaled bounding box for the check. Returns false if the sprite is hidden or costume dimensions have not been set.
      Parameters:
      mouseX - mouse X position in Scratch coordinates
      mouseY - mouse Y position in Scratch coordinates
      Returns:
      true if the mouse is within the sprite's bounding box, false otherwise

    • sayForTime

      public void sayForTime(String text, int seconds)
      Makes the sprite display a speech bubble for a set duration. The timing is handled by the Interpreter via waitUntil — this method just sets the text immediately; the Interpreter clears it after the delay.
      Parameters:
      text - the text to display
      seconds - how long to display it (handled by the Interpreter)
